newsitem.title: INDIA: India declares week-long ceasefire in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: India declares week-long ceasefire in Kashmir.

text.p: The Indian army on Monday declared a week-long unilateral ceasefire in its operations against separatist guerrillas in troubled Kashmir.

"From tomorrow (Tuesday) we are not going to carry out cordon and search operations or anti-militant operations until the 11th of February," Corps Commander Lieutenant General Jagdish Singh Dhillon told a news conference.
"For the next week security forces will disturb nobody so that people can enjoy and celebrate Eid," he said.

Last February the army declared a 24-hour ceasefire on Eid al-Fitr, a Moslem holiday marking the end of the fasting month of Ramadan. This year it will be celebrated on Sunday in Jammu and Kashmir, mostly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state.

Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have been killed in insurgency-related violence since a separatist revolt erupted in the Himalayan region in 1990. Thousands of soldiers, along with local police and paramilitary troops, are stationed in the state.
Dhillon, who is also security adviser to the state government, said Kashmiri militants could celebrate Eid al-Fitr with family and friends provided they did not carry weapons.
"Our own militants who are from our own people, are welcome to move around, meet their friends, families, and they are advised not to carry arms," Dhillon said.
"Foreign militants do not belong to our country so we are not going to leave them (alone)," he said, adding that more than 400 foreign militants have been killed in the past three years.
India accuses Pakistan of arming and training Kashmiri and foreign militants. Islamabad says it provides only diplomatic and moral support.
More than a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir.
